proof_summary: Take \(n=1408\) and exhaust all \(1\le k<1408\): after computing each exponent \(\phi(1408-k)/2\), modular exponentiation supplies a proper divisor of \((k+1)^{\phi(1408-k)/2}-k\) in every nontrivial case, while the remaining terminal cases give values below \(2\). Thus no admissible \(k\) yields a prime.
